title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_1LC1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_1LC1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Seen from the left end, its tape is mostly two long runs of the word 11010 with a marker between them; seen from the right end, it is one long run of 11000 with about as many words, after a short disordered stretch. Its near-twin 1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_0LE1LF does the same.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps; the C simulator shows none in 109. How the disordered stretch evolves is not yet understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,397 cells have been visited and 1,981 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Tape shape
claims.text: At the last side switches before 109 steps the tape is, at the left end, 0 (10)^23 (11010)^306 1 10 0 10 (11010)^359 10 10 11010 1 10 0 10 1 10 (step 995,707,723); at the right end, … (11000)^665 1 11000 0000 (11000)^2 1 10 after a disordered stretch of 49 cells (step 996,668,901). The two runs of 11010 at the left (301 + 362, then 306 + 359) add up to the run of 11000 at the right (663 + 1 and 665).

claims.title: A twin
claims.text: 1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_0LE1LF and 1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_1LC1LF behave alike: the first 1,241 side switches (all of the first machine's in 109 steps) fall on the same sides with exactly the same widths; the second machine is faster and reaches 1,319 switches in 109 steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.324). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328).

claims.title: Growth like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: After step 5·10<sup>8</sup>: 276 side switches, 1,802,517 steps apart on average (≈ 0.156·w<sup>2</sup>, w = 3396), about 2.5 cells of width per switch; fitted width exponent 0.325 after step 10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is D reading 1. D is entered only from C reading 0, which writes 0 and moves left. So a halt is exactly 1 C>0: C on a 0 with a 1 to its left.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The run structure holds at the switches printed; what the disordered stretch does, and whether it can produce the halting pattern, are open.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The head shuttles between the ends, rewriting runs of 11010 into one run of 11000 and back; a trip costs about the width squared, for a few cells of growth, so the width grows like the cube root of the time.

facts.text: Width of the tape at its last extension before step 10<sup>9</sup>.
Side switches in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: Runs of words rewritten end to end
html: The tape at the last side switches:

The two runs of 11010 at the left (301 + 362, then 306 + 359) add up to the run of 11000 at the right (663 + 1 and 665). The left end and the right end carry short disordered stretches; everything else is runs of a single word.

1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_0LE1LF and 1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_1LC1LF behave alike: the first 1,241 side switches (all of the first machine's in 109 steps) fall on the same sides with exactly the same widths; the second machine is faster and reaches 1,319 switches in 109 steps.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. After step 5·108 there are 276 side switches (extensions of the tape on the other side from the last one), on average 1,802,517 steps apart, which is about 0.156·w2 for the final width w = 3396; each adds about 2.5 cells to the width. A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. The fitted exponent of the width after step 107 is 0.325.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.324). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.328).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,397 cells (2,223 left of the start, 548 right), with a density of 1s of 0.583.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LF_1LC0RE_0LD1LC_1LA---_0RB1RA_0LE1LF: 8,345,589 configurations, the last at step 8,345,588 here and step 10,000,000 there

family: runs of 11010 and 11000 rewritten end to end
summary: Two long runs of the word 11010 at the left end turn into one run of 11000 at the right end, with about as many words, next to a short disordered stretch; the head shuttles between the ends and the width grows like t^(1/3).
